policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 13 Feb close (1x4 3.73, 3x6 3.51, 6x9 3.38, 9x12 3.35 vs WIBOR 3M 3.86) price roughly 50bp of NBP cuts within 12 months. The MPC held at 4.00% on 4 Feb; the statement says CPI may fall in Q1 and stay consistent with the target in coming quarters. Glapiński (5 Feb): a March cut if the projection shows nothing worrying; 3.5% possible as the end-point. Most MPC members now point to a 25bp cut in March (Kotecki, Masłowska, Zarzecki, Wnorowski); Litwiniuk floated 50bp in April instead. January flash CPI came in at 2.2% (1.9% expected, 13 Feb); ING (16 Feb) still sees a 25bp March cut as 'essentially settled'.
policy.risk_text: January CPI (2.2%) beat forecasts before the basket revision; if the March projection disappoints, the cut slips to April (Dąbrowski) and the front end backs up; oil spikes on Iran and US tariff changes move the long end.

cpi.m: Jan flash (GUS, 13 Feb; 2025 weights, revision mid-March); Dec 2.4%

macro.projection_text: NBP November 2025 projection: CPI 2.9% (2026), 2.5% (2027); the March 2026 projection comes with the 3-4 Mar MPC.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit ~7.0% of GDP; 2026 budget deficit cap PLN 271.7bn (in force; at the Constitutional Tribunal for follow-up review), gross borrowing needs ~PLN 690bn; the Sejm passed the SAFE defence-loan law (13 Feb), and SAFE loans sit outside the Polish public-debt definition (MoF).
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~33% (11 Feb) financed; budget accounts PLN 183bn at end-January; Fitch reviews Poland on 27 Feb (after the close) and Moody's on 20 Mar, both with negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP held at 4.00% on 14 Jan and 4 Feb; January flash CPI 2.2% y/y (13 Feb; 1.9% expected); 2025 GDP grew 3.6% (30 Jan); Q4 +4.0% y/y (12 Feb). Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 13-15 Feb: January flash CPI 2.2% y/y (1.9% expected, +0.6% m/m; on 2025 weights, the basket revision comes in mid-March); December current account -EUR 1.7bn (-1.1bn expected); the Sejm passed the SAFE defence-loan law. Abroad: US January CPI 2.4% (2.5% expected), core 2.5%; ~63bp of 2026 Fed cuts priced; CNB minutes show two members leaning towards a cut.

calendar.plan_text: MoF February plan (30 Jan): sale auctions on 11, 18 and 25 Feb (PLN 7-12bn each), no switch auction, a 33-week T-bill auction on 6 Feb; January sales were ~PLN 41.6bn incl. additional sales. BGK placed PLN 1bn of FWA0931 (Armed Forces Support Fund) privately (29-30 Jan). JPY 211.6bn priced on 6 Feb (3Y 1.88%, 5Y 2.22%, 10Y 2.90%, 20Y 3.65%); 33-week T-bills PLN 2.6bn at 3.529%. 11 Feb: PLN 11.9bn sold vs 25.8bn demand (cover 2.18) plus 1.38bn additional; OK0128 unsold; stop yields PS0131 4.298%, DS1033 4.732%, DS1035 5.035%, WS0437 5.148%.
calendar.timing_text: Within each auction week of the Aug 2025-Feb 2026 sample, yields drifted lower into the auction and the auction-day close was the cheapest point relative to the preceding session, so new buying is best executed at the auction-day close (18 and 25 Feb). February covers so far: 2.18x (11 Feb). The 3-4 Mar MPC with the new projection is the next event; a 25bp cut is the consensus.

facts.core_text: Regime: the NBP paused at 4.00% with ~50bp more priced, the ECB is on hold at 2.00%, the Fed holds into June, the BoE eases gradually, the CNB and MNB are on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 56bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 222bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 13 Feb close). US CPI 2.4% (13 Feb) revived Fed-cut pricing.

Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).
12 Feb BGK auction: PLN 3.39bn sold vs 6.35bn demand plus 0.75bn additional.
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
